experiment: E15 deep-history first capture: what a commit-graph file would change
decision: no change; a cold capture at 300,000 commits spends about 0.84 of its 1.19 s in a walk that reads every commit object, which a commit-graph file can replace for topology only (0.84 s to 0.08 to 0.09 s in libgit2's own walk), but libgit2 1.9 reads neither the generation-data chunk git 2.56 writes by default nor a split chain, and the capture also reads every commit's message and author, so the gain needs a commit-graph reader of Trunk's own and facts read after the first page
scope: backend only, a release probe linking trunk-git at 08fbdebf and git2 0.21 (libgit2 1.9.7 vendored); timed in-process; not the app's open, not the frontend
comparativeVerdict: the version-1 commit-graph walk is faster in every reading (max 106.8 ms against min 830.4 ms without a readable file); the generation-data file and the chain match the no-file walk (835.2 to 850.7 ms against 830.4 to 856.4 ms); disabling strict hash verification saved 2 to 10% of the capture
machine: Apple M5 Pro, 48 GB, macOS, release profile with debug = 1, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 for the build only

builds.probe: a scratch crate holding the probe below, with a path dependency on src-tauri/git at 08fbdebf

fixture.build: git init <dir>; python3 generator.py 300000 | git -C <dir> fast-import --quiet, the E13 generator (docs/performance-data/deep-history-layout-2026-11-18.json)

variants.repo-cg: git commit-graph write --reachable (git 2.56.0 default, chunks OIDF OIDL CDAT GDA2)
variants.repo-cg1: git -c commitGraph.generationVersion=1 commit-graph write --reachable (chunks OIDF OIDL CDAT)

procedure: each mode is one process run on one variant: capture = trunk_git::graph::capture_remembering with an empty memo; revwalk = libgit2 revwalk TOPOLOGICAL|TIME over refs/*, counted; unsorted = the same walk unsorted; topology = unsorted walk plus find_commit reading parents and time; facts = unsorted walk plus find_commit and the summary, body, author name and email copied as the capture copies them. NOSTRICT=1 sets git2::opts::strict_hash_verification(false) first. git rev-list --topo-order --all timed with /usr/bin/time for comparison.
profile: sample(1) over five unsorted walks of repo-cg: 594 of the walk's samples under git_commit_list_parse were in git_odb_read, 509 in zlib inflate, 85 in git_odb__hashobj; libgit2's commit_graph.c returns 'unrecognized chunk ID' for any chunk but OIDF, OIDL, CDAT, EDGE, BIDX and BDAT, and opens only objects/info/commit-graph
limitations: one generated history shape whose commit objects are small; real commits carry longer messages, which raises the facts share
no real repository of this depth was available; the deepest on this machine has 5,073 commits
every repository past 100 commits under ~/code on this machine (11) keeps a split chain, none a single file, so the chain result is the representative one here
fresh clones carry no commit-graph until git gc or git maintenance writes one
